AlphaLensReferenceLocal prediction

Local prediction

AlphaLens can predict a protein complex from sequences or UniProt IDs, or re-predict an interface you select on the plot, with AlphaFold 2 or AlphaFold 3 on your own computer: an Apple Silicon Mac, or Linux with an NVIDIA GPU. The prediction runs in the background, so ChimeraX stays responsive, and the result opens in an AlphaLens window of its own. Windows and Intel Macs are not supported yet.

Predictions run LocalFold by Sergey Ovchinnikov, with quantized copies of the AlphaFold parameters, so its models can differ slightly from those of AlphaFold itself. A confident score is not proof of an interaction.

Setup

You need:

  • Mac: Apple Silicon, macOS 13 or newer, and the Xcode Command Line Tools (install them with xcode-select --install).
  • Linux: x86_64 with an NVIDIA GPU from the T4 on (Turing, Ampere, Ada, Hopper, Blackwell) and its driver; while setup runs, the CUDA 12 toolkit (nvcc, cuBLAS; 12.8 or newer for Blackwell) and g++ on the PATH (on a cluster, load the CUDA module before starting ChimeraX); git, curl, gzip, sha256sum, and glibc 2.28 or newer.

No Python environment is needed. The first time, the button in the prediction dialog reads Install & Predict: it downloads and builds the prediction engine in the background, then predicts. Cancel setup stops it; after an error, click the button again. Update & Predict means that a new AlphaLens needs a newer engine; it is rebuilt once.

On a cluster, run the first prediction on a GPU node. The engine is built for the GPU it was set up on: on a GPU of another generation (A100 and H100 nodes sharing a home folder, for example) AlphaLens refuses to predict and says how to build it again.

The first prediction with each AlphaFold version also downloads its parameters, about 80 MB for AlphaFold 2 and 280 MB for AlphaFold 3, and keeps them for later. AlphaFold 3 parameters are downloaded only after you accept Google DeepMind's terms of use and prohibited use policy in the dialog.

Predict from sequences, FASTA or UniProt IDs

  1. Choose Tools → Structure Prediction → AlphaLens Prediction, or run alphalens predict. No structure needs to be open.
  2. Paste one of:
    • a sequence (line breaks are fine);
    • FASTA entries, one chain each;
    • UniProt IDs separated by spaces: accessions (P69905), isoforms (P05067-2) or entry names (RNBR_BACAM). P69905 P68871 gives the two subunits of human hemoglobin;
    • AlphaPulldown notation: P0A836:1-100+P0AGE9 (a region of one protein and a whole second one), P69905:2 (two copies), Q8I2G6:2:1-100:150-200 (two copies of two regions).
  3. Click Load sequences and check the chains in the table (hover for the sequence). A range such as 50-157 (first and last residue, counted from 1) predicts part of a chain; 1-100,150-200 predicts two regions as one chain with a gap (see Regions with a gap).
  4. Choose AlphaFold 2 or AlphaFold 3.
  5. Choose an alignment: an A3M file whose first sequence is exactly the chosen sequences, precomputed AlphaPulldown features, or Search remotely if uncached, which sends the sequences to the ColabFold MSA server. Alignments are kept, so the same sequences are not searched twice.
  6. Click Predict.

UniProt IDs are looked up at UniProt; only the IDs are sent. A residue written X is predicted as an unknown residue. U, O, B, Z and J are refused, with what to write instead.

Re-predict a selected interface

  1. In an AlphaLens window, drag a box across the interface between two chains (a block off the diagonal). Either side of the box can span several chains.
  2. Right-click the plot and choose Re-predict selected interface….
  3. Choose the flanks, the residues added on each side of the box (10 by default; they stop at the ends of chains and at gaps).
  4. Choose the alignment. Reuse and crop the source MSA is chosen for you when the MSA the prediction was made with is at hand:
  5. an A3M of all its chains beside the model (LocalFold, ColabFold);
  6. the features.pkl of an AlphaFold 2 run;
  7. the msas folder of an AlphaFold Server download;
  8. the <name>_data.json of an AlphaFold 3 run (also compressed, .json.xz);
  9. for AlphaPulldown, the proteins' features in the features folder beside predictions, as AlphaPulldownSnakemake writes them.

You can also give an A3M for exactly the cropped sequences, use precomputed AlphaPulldown features from elsewhere (the protein IDs come from the folder name, such as Q15014+Q9NV56), or search remotely. 5. Click Predict. When Predict is greyed out, the line above the buttons says what is missing.

The result opens superposed on the source's first selected chain; the source is not used as a template. Only proteins are predicted: ligands and nucleic acids in the box are left out, and a box with a modified residue is refused.

A crop changes the problem: confidence can go up or down without the structure getting better. Keep whole domains in the box, and compare a few seeds and crop sizes.

Is it the same interface?

The report, the dialog and the heading of the result's window compare the new interface with the source by DockQ (Basu & Wallner 2016), for each pair of chains:

Interface vs source: DockQ 0.92 · high: same interface
  A–B: 44 of 46 source contacts kept (Fnat 0.96), 3 new; interface RMSD 0.7 Å; B 1.3 Å from its source place with A superposed

DockQ of 0.80 and above is high (the same interface), 0.49 medium (similar), 0.23 acceptable (partly the same); below that the interface is a different one. The source is a prediction too, so DockQ says how alike the two interfaces are, not which one is right. Long disordered tails can make the last distance large while the interface agrees; the contacts kept (Fnat) and the interface RMSD show that.

The report also gives ipTM, the mean PAE and pLDDT over the selected residues (without the flanks) in the source and in the new prediction, and their contacts with P ≥ 0.5, strongest first. These are probabilities that two residues are in contact, not that the proteins interact.

Compare with source, in the dialog and in the result's right-click menu, shows the re-prediction colored by chain with the same residues of the source in grey, and hides the rest of the source; click it again to restore both. The right-click menu can also superpose the re-prediction on the source's first selected chain, or on the backbone of the source interface.

Regions with a gap

Two regions of one protein, 1-100,150-200, are predicted as one chain with a gap, as AlphaPulldown does with P1:1-100:150-200: AlphaFold knows that the two segments are far apart in the sequence, instead of joining them or treating them as two molecules. A box across a gap in a model (an AlphaPulldown region, or missing residues) keeps the gap. The dialog lists the segments, for example "A: 98 residues in 2 segments".

Precomputed AlphaPulldown features

Precomputed AlphaPulldown features takes each chain's alignments from an AlphaPulldown feature file named by its UniProt ID, so no alignment search runs. Features from is the public AlphaPulldown feature database at EMBL, with AlphaFold 2 features for 16 proteomes and AlphaFold 3 features for two (only the IDs are sent, and the files are kept), or a folder of your own AlphaPulldown features. AlphaFold 3 uses the <ID>_af3_input.json files when every chain has one. Templates are not used, and the features of a whole complex are refused.

Settings, large inputs and time limits

Settings (its summary line shows the values) holds the recycles, the seed, the AlphaFold 3 diffusion steps and samples, a time limit, the results folder and the engine. Each prediction gets a new random seed unless you untick New random seed for each prediction and give one.

There is no size limit. Above 1,024 residues in all, the dialog warns that the prediction may be slow or may not fit in the GPU's memory; you can still predict. The time limit (none by default) covers the whole job, including the alignment search. Cancel job, or closing the dialog, stops a prediction. A remote alignment search can wait in a queue for minutes; reusing an alignment is fast.

Results

Each prediction is saved in a folder of its own under the results folder (by default ~/.local/share/alphalens/predictions): the structure fold.pdb (and fold_sample<k>.pdb for the other AlphaFold 3 samples), its confidences, the alignment, region_contacts.csv with the contacts of a complex, and prediction_report.txt. Residues keep the numbering of the input: the source's chains and residue numbers for a re-predicted interface, so #1/A:120 and #2/A:120 are the same residue, and UniProt numbering for UniProt IDs.

The result's window has every view except Spread, which needs the full distogram. Open a result again like any prediction, alphalens open <folder> (rank 1, rank 2, … for the other AF3 samples). Prediction report…, in the dialog and in the result's right-click menu, shows the report again. The dialog keeps a history of its messages and reports, which also go to the log.

The AlphaFold 2 parameters are by Google DeepMind, under CC BY 4.0; AlphaLens includes the AlphaFold 2 multimer distogram head, so that predictions have contact probabilities.
